subject: Residency confirmation — ephemeral cache export and subprocessor controls
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Alex Henderson <alex.henderson@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-22T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Residency confirmation — ephemeral cache export and subprocessor controls

Alex — thanks for the time last week. A quick follow-up so we can close out the technical asks on residency for the upcoming pilot. Attached is a short checklist (residency-MAP-questions.pdf) — the items below are the ones legal/infra raised as blockers for production. Can you confirm or indicate what you need from us to accept the commitments?

Key asks:
- Persistent storage: can you confirm that production customer data for EU-tagged projects will be pinned to EU-backed persistent stores (no permanent cross-border writes)?
- Transient/ephemeral caches: we use short-lived KV caches to accelerate inference (prefix caching & KV warm-ups). Does your compliance team require that these caches never transit outside the EU, or is a documented transient cache-warmup window acceptable? If acceptable, what's the max window?
- Subprocessors: we need to publish the minimal subprocessor roster in the DPA addendum. Any objections to the two named partners below (CloudFabric Ltd. — EU compute; EdgeAnalytica — cache optimization) being listed and bound to EU tenancy for EU customers?
- Audit evidence: Acme needs a short artifact (SOC2 control mapping or attestation) that region-binding for persistent stores is enforced and that transient cache egress is logged.

Proposed next steps: 1) quick confirmation on the three bullets; 2) we’ll circulate DPA addendum language (legal looped in); 3) target DocuSign by end of next week if everything matches.

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Blake
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference

From: Alex Henderson <alex.henderson@acmecorp.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Legal <legal@acmecorp.com>
Date: 2026-08-22T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Residency confirmation — ephemeral cache export and subprocessor controls

Jordan — thanks, clear list. A few quick answers and constraints from our side: 

1) Persistent storage: Acme’s security policy requires production customer data for EU customers to remain in EU persistent stores (no outbound replication without explicit, auditable exception). We need that encoded in the DPA.

2) Transient/ephemeral caches: We are generally comfortable with short warming windows for caches as long as they are strictly transient and auditable. Our security team suggested a conservative maximum of 120 seconds for any cross-region cache warming or KV prefill operations; beyond that we need prior approval. We will accept a documented exception process for short cold-starts.

3) Subprocessors: We require the subprocessor roster and a contractual guarantee that any subprocessor handling EU-tagged workload will operate in EU tenancy. We need to review contracts for CloudFabric Ltd. and EdgeAnalytica.

4) Audit evidence: Please provide a mapping of Redwood controls to our SOC2/ISO controls; if you can provide a short attestation that region-binding for persistent stores is enforced and a sample log extract showing cache-warmup egress events (anonymized), that should suffice for our initial approval.

I’ve attached Acme's security expectations doc so you can align the DPA language. If you can circulate proposed DPA text, I’ll route to our legal and security reviewers.

—Alex
Alex Henderson
Director of Cloud Security, AcmeCorp
---
Attachment: acme-security-expectations.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Henderson <alex.henderson@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-22T13:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Residency confirmation — ephemeral cache export and subprocessor controls

Alex — appreciate the clarity and the attachment. Looping Neha from legal to propose firm language. High level from product/infra: 

- Persistent storage: Redwood confirms that for EU-tagged projects, persistent customer data (object stores, DB snapshots, training artifacts) will be written to and retained in EU-backed persistent stores controlled under our EU tenancy. No automatic replication to non-EU locations will occur unless an auditable, customer-authorized exception is granted.

- Transient caches: Our serving runtime uses two cache tiers: (a) hot in-region KV cache (primary), and (b) opportunistic prefill/replication used only for cold-start mitigation. For EU customers we can enforce a policy that prefill/replication to non-EU nodes is blocked by default; however, to avoid long cold starts we propose the following operational exception that we can encode in the addendum:
  - Transient cache-warmup window for cross-region prefill: up to 90 seconds by default for cold-starts; any single warming event exceeding 120 seconds will trigger an alert and require approval.
  - All prefill/replication events will be logged (idempotent request id, timestamp, origin region, destination region) and retained in audit logs for 90 days.

- Subprocessors: We can list CloudFabric Ltd. and EdgeAnalytica in the addendum and include a contractual clause requiring EU-only tenancy and data access restrictions for EU-tagged workloads. If Acme legal wants copies of the subprocessor SLAs, we can produce redacted contract exhibits under NDA.

Next step: Neha, can you draft a short DPA addendum snippet we can share back to Alex? If Acme agrees to the 90s default prefill with 120s alert threshold and the logging/retention commitment, we’ll push to DocuSign.

Thanks — Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Alex Henderson <alex.henderson@acmecorp.com>
Date: 2026-08-23T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Residency confirmation — ephemeral cache export and subprocessor controls

Alex / Marissa / Jordan — attaching a brief DPA addendum draft and the proposed clause text. Key points we recommend including in the addendum (plain language for review):

1) Region pinning: "Redwood shall ensure that persistent customer content for EU-tagged environments is stored exclusively within EU-backed persistent stores and shall not be written to non-EU persistent storage unless Customer provides a documented, auditable exception."

2) Transient cache egress: "Redwood's serving runtime may perform transient cache prefill/replication to mitigate cold-start latency. For EU-tagged environments Redwood will: (a) default to in-region caching; (b) permit cross-region prefill only as an operationally-defined exception bounded to a default maximum of 90 seconds per event; (c) treat events exceeding 120 seconds as an incident that requires Customer notification and approval; and (d) log all prefill events (request id, origin, destination, duration) with retention for 90 days."

3) Subprocessors: list CloudFabric Ltd. and EdgeAnalytica with the annex that states: "For EU-tagged workloads Redwood will ensure that these subprocessors operate using EU tenancy for processing activities and agree to obligations substantially similar to Redwood's DPA obligations."

I’ve attached dpa-addendum-region-pinning.docx (redline + clean copy). Alex, if you mark any edits or flag specific phrasing we’ll iterate quickly. If that text is acceptable, Jordan/Marissa — we can feed this into DocuSign and attach the subprocessor exhibits under NDA as requested.

-Neha
Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

- Persistent storage: EU-only for EU-tagged projects, no automatic cross-border persistent replication without customer exception.
- Transient cache prefill: default in-region; cross-region prefill allowed only as a narrow operational exception (default max 90s per event; >120s triggers notification/approval). All prefill events logged and retained for 90 days.
- Subprocessors: CloudFabric Ltd. and EdgeAnalytica will be listed; both will be contractually bound to EU tenancy requirements for EU workloads.
